dimension_justifications.soundness: The reported decomposition arithmetic is internally consistent, the finite-pool recorded-realization target is explicitly distinguished from decoder- and population-level expectations, and causal claims are mostly avoided. However, the central score is not operationally defined, the treatment and samples cannot be reconstructed, the bootstrap brackets lack an inferential target compatible with the stated fixed-pool estimand, and none of the empirical records is included. Consequently, only transcription arithmetic and scope statements—not the empirical findings—are verifiable.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The manuscript is unusually transparent about its evidence boundary, clearly separates central, secondary, and ancillary analyses, is anonymous, includes an AI-assistance disclosure, and uses only four main-text pages before references. Verification remains obstructed by opaque evidence IDs, unavailable source locations, undefined secondary quantities, and insufficient displayed precision in Table 3.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The strongest defensible contribution is an estimand clarification and cautious audit of source-reported summaries. There is no independently supported empirical result, new validated measure, reproducible intervention, or inferential comparison, and the prompt-length/masked-diffusion literature search is acknowledged as incomplete.

paper_summary: The paper juxtaposes a source-reported observational high-versus-low prompt-length difference of +0.2227 with a source-reported 400-item paired fixed-filler contrast of -0.0075 for a cross-level mean recorded-score-minus-answer-correctness quantity. It defines the latter as conditional on a finite pool and one stored decode per arm, treats the magnitude comparison as descriptive, declines causal and decoder-average conclusions, and demotes source-labelled Brier/NLL values and MATH500 judge variants to secondary numerical scenarios. All empirical records, treatment artifacts, score construction, and analysis code are absent.
strongest_verified_contribution: The paper correctly formalizes and explains that a paired statistic conditional on one finite pool and one recorded decode realization is not an expectation over items, decoder randomness, filler choices, or prompt constructions. Its reported component differences also satisfy the stated subtraction identities, subject to transcription and rounding.
strengths: The distinction among observational association, a paired recorded-realization contrast, and causal or decoder-average effects is explicit and technically appropriate.
The paper correctly states that comparing -0.0075 and +0.2227 across different samples and estimands is descriptive only and supplies no joint inference.

The commit score is not presented as a validated answer-correctness probability; accordingly, Brier/NLL are conservatively described as source-labelled numerical diagnostics rather than established calibration measures.
The MATH500 purposive-anchor band is explicitly identified as a scenario range rather than a confidence interval, and no cross-benchmark confirmation is claimed.
Missing records and protocol details are disclosed prominently. The PDF is anonymous, within the nine-page main-text limit, and contains an AI-assistance disclosure.
questions: What exact algorithm maps a decode trace to the scalar s_iaω: which committed token or tokens are used, at what step, with what aggregation and weighting, and what forecast event is the score intended to represent?

What statistical population or repeated-sampling target gives the problem-level bootstrap brackets confidence-interval semantics when Δ_P,ω is defined for a fixed, fully recorded pool and realization?
How were the 400 items selected, do they overlap the natural-strata sample, and was any quantitative criterion for 'comparably large' specified before observing the results?
What are the literal filler, insertion position, serialized Short and Long prompts, tokenizer revision, verified token difference, model revision, decode settings, and arm execution order?
What exact formulas, clipping conventions, aggregation rules, and score-label pairings produced the Brier- and NLL-labelled values, and what quantity do the two MATH500 convention values estimate?

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Introduction lines 24-26 and 54-58; PDF p. 2, Section 2 'What is missing'; PDF p. 4, Section 7; reviewer-safe experiment registry A32-X1--A32-X3 and repository inventory
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript says every empirical number is source-reported and cannot be independently verified. E1--E4 are explicitly opaque references to missing records, while all three reported experiments are registered as not rerun. No per-item observations, prompts, traces, labels, judge outputs, interval inputs, or analysis implementation is included.
issues.why_it_matters: The only checkable empirical content is arithmetic among transcribed summaries. Pairing, measurement validity, treatment fidelity, item selection, reported intervals, and even the underlying observations cannot be assessed. An ICLR empirical conclusion cannot rest solely on unavailable source records, even when the limitation is candidly disclosed.
issues.required_fix: Provide a blind, immutable artifact containing the item-level records and stable evidence-ID crosswalk for E1--E4, exact inputs and outputs, analysis code, and table-generation procedure; alternatively rerun the smallest central paired experiment under a frozen reproducible protocol and restrict the paper to that verified result.
issues.verification_test: From a clean environment, resolve every evidence ID to a hash-verified file and independently regenerate Tables 2 and 3, all brackets, the MATH scenario values, counts, exclusions, and decomposition identities without manually entering manuscript numbers.
issues.evidence_needed: Item-level natural-strata and paired-arm records; prompt and decode traces; correctness labels; manifests and selection rules; bootstrap inputs; judge and anchor records; executable analysis and table-generation code; immutable hashes and an ID-to-file crosswalk.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Section 1, lines 36-42; PDF p. 2, Section 3, definition of s_iaω and D_P,ω; PDF p. 3, Table 3 and 'Score-based loss diagnostics'; method provenance A32-M1 and A32-M5
issues.observed_evidence: The scalar s_iaω is described only as a recorded commit score. The paper does not define which token, commit step, aggregation, weighting, normalization, or forecast event creates one item-level scalar. It separately acknowledges that token-to-answer aggregation, score extraction, Brier/NLL implementation, and NLL clipping are absent.
issues.why_it_matters: Different plausible constructions—last answer-token score, mean over all generated tokens, length-weighted token mean, minimum score, or another readout—define different estimands and can respond differently to added prompt tokens. Without an answer-event interpretation, Brier and NLL also lack their usual proper-scoring-rule semantics, although the paper appropriately avoids claiming those semantics.
issues.required_fix: Specify an executable mathematical mapping from each decode trace to s_iaω, including token scope, step, aggregation and weighting, range, normalization, and the event being scored. Give exact formulas and clipping for every secondary loss, and justify or explicitly disclaim the relation between the commit event and final-answer correctness.
issues.verification_test: Apply the specification to fixed synthetic traces that distinguish alternative aggregation choices, then reproduce every item-level score and all arm-level score, D, Brier, and NLL summaries from the released traces.
issues.evidence_needed: Formal score/readout definition, reference implementation, unit-test fixtures, raw decode traces, per-item derived scores, and Brier/NLL formulas.

issues.location: PDF p. 2, Section 3 equations and 'Uncertainty record'; PDF p. 3, Tables 2-3; claim-evidence map A32-C2
issues.observed_evidence: The central target is defined conditional on the complete fixed pool P and recorded realization ω, for which the empirical mean is fixed once records exist. Nevertheless, bootstrap brackets are reported beside it without a specified sampling population, resampling estimand, coverage target, code, or replicates. The manuscript calls them 'brackets,' while the claim-evidence map calls the filler bracket a CI.
issues.why_it_matters: A problem bootstrap can describe an empirical resampling distribution or uncertainty for a superpopulation target, but it is not a confidence interval for an already fixed finite-pool quantity without an additional sampling model. It also omits decoder-run uncertainty by construction. The current interval therefore has no coherent inferential semantics tied to the stated estimand.
issues.required_fix: Choose and state the target explicitly. For the conditional finite-pool estimand, report the exact point contrast and treat resampling spreads as descriptive. For population inference, define the item-sampling mechanism and superpopulation estimand, justify the resampling unit, and label the resulting interval accordingly. Estimate decoder variation separately with deterministic replay evidence or repeated paired decodes.
issues.verification_test: Given released rows and code, recompute the interval using the declared resampling unit and confirm that its target, conditioning set, and sources of variation match the manuscript label; test coverage by simulation if confidence-interval language is retained.
issues.evidence_needed: Sampling-frame definition, formal inferential estimand, bootstrap algorithm, rows, seeds and replicates, interval-construction code, and repeated-decode evidence for any decoder-average uncertainty claim.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Introduction lines 43-46; PDF p. 2, Sections 2-3; PDF p. 3, Section 4.2 lines 148-156; PDF p. 5, Conclusion lines 222-227
issues.observed_evidence: The natural-strata and filler estimates use different unknown item pools and different targets, with no overlap map, covariance, common-sample natural contrast, joint uncertainty calculation, or prespecified definition of 'comparably large.' The paper acknowledges these facts but still presents whether filler can 'account operationally' for the natural gap as its central diagnostic question.
issues.why_it_matters: The numbers support only the literal observation that the reported absolute point estimates differ. They cannot determine whether the filler effect is small relative to the natural association on comparable items, nor whether filler operationally accounts for any portion of that association. The careful noncausal wording prevents a false causal conclusion but does not make the central diagnostic decision-ready.
issues.required_fix: Either reframe the contribution strictly as an audit and descriptive juxtaposition, removing account/comparability language, or evaluate both quantities on an aligned sample under a prespecified comparison statistic or margin with joint uncertainty. A factorial content/filler/position design would be required for component attribution.
issues.verification_test: On a preregistered common item manifest, compute both contrasts and a declared comparison such as their difference or magnitude ratio, propagate their covariance with an appropriate paired procedure, and apply the specified margin without post hoc threshold selection.
issues.evidence_needed: Common item identities, overlap map, aligned natural and intervention measurements, prespecified comparability criterion, joint analysis code, and preferably factorial intervention records.

issues.location: PDF p. 2, Section 2 'What is missing'; PDF p. 3, Section 4.2 lines 131-145; PDF p. 4, Section 7 lines 200-212; experiment registry A32-X2 and method provenance A32-M3
issues.observed_evidence: The literal filler, insertion rule, prompt serialization, tokenizer and dose check, 400-item selection rule, item pairing, model/tokenizer revision, gate implementation, arm execution order, and decode configuration are absent. Thus '+37-token fixed filler at NFE=64' is a source description rather than an inspectable treatment.
issues.why_it_matters: It cannot be verified that the arms differ only in the intended operation, that the token dose is 37 under the actual tokenizer, that the filler is semantically inert, that NFE is held fixed, or that the same items are correctly paired. Any of these failures could change the interpretation from a length intervention to a content, formatting, position, selection, or execution-order effect.
issues.required_fix: Release the complete frozen treatment protocol and fixtures: literal filler, insertion location, exact serialized prompts, tokenizer/model hashes, token-ID diffs, item manifest, exclusions, pairing keys, gate logic, arm order, decode seed/state, and fixed-NFE launcher configuration.
issues.verification_test: Independently serialize and tokenize every pair; assert identical item content and settings outside the declared insertion; verify exactly 37 added token IDs, NFE=64 in both arms, unique paired identifiers, no duplicate or post-treatment exclusions, and execution logs matching the frozen configuration.
issues.evidence_needed: Prompt fixtures, token-ID outputs, model/tokenizer revisions, paired manifest and selection rule, decode configuration and logs, gate implementation, randomization/order record, and integrity hashes.

issues.location: PDF p. 3, Table 3 and surrounding component-accounting discussion
issues.observed_evidence: Table 3 gives arm means to three decimals but differences and D values to four decimals. Consequently, displayed identities do not reproduce exactly: 0.630-0.703=-0.073 rather than -0.0724, and 0.543-0.630=-0.087 rather than -0.0875. Rounding is a plausible explanation, but it is unstated and cannot be checked against rows.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper presents arithmetic auditability as one of the few verifiable properties. Insufficient displayed precision makes even that audit appear inconsistent and obscures whether differences were computed from unrounded paired values.
issues.required_fix: Display sufficient precision for all component means or state explicitly that contrasts were computed from unrounded item-level values. Prefer a table-generation check that verifies each displayed decomposition within the declared rounding tolerance.
issues.verification_test: Regenerate the table from item rows and assert that D(a)=mean(s_a)-mean(y_a) and Δ=D(L)-D(S)=Δs-Δy before rounding, then confirm the rendered values agree within the stated tolerance.
issues.evidence_needed: Unrounded component means, item-level rows, table-generation code, and a documented rounding rule.

issues.location: PDF p. 4, Section 6, especially lines 181-196; citation lock 'remaining_unverified_scope'
issues.observed_evidence: The included citation lock verifies three neighboring prompt-variation studies and several signed-calibration-summary sources, but both the manuscript and lock acknowledge that the broader prompt-length-specific and masked-diffusion uncertainty search is incomplete.
issues.why_it_matters: The contribution is framed as operation-specific rather than methodological. Its distinctness and significance therefore depend heavily on whether closer prompt-length, filler-control, diffusion-decoding, or token-score studies exist; the current snapshot cannot establish that positioning.
issues.required_fix: Complete a documented primary-source search focused on prompt length, content-free fillers, fixed-compute diffusion decoding, token-commit uncertainty, and same-item prompt perturbations, then revise the contribution boundary against the closest work without claiming uniqueness from an incomplete search.
issues.verification_test: For every novelty or closest-work statement, trace the claim to verified primary-source passages and compare task, intervention, score construction, pairing, compute control, and estimand in a closest-work matrix.
issues.evidence_needed: Search protocol, candidate bibliography, primary-source metadata and support checks, and a closest-work comparison matrix.

ethics_concerns: No direct ethics concern is apparent from the frozen snapshot. If the missing MATH500 judge or human-anchor records involved new human annotation, the final artifact should disclose recruitment, consent, compensation, privacy handling, and applicable review status; the current snapshot does not establish that such data collection occurred.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by isolated AI subagent A32-R01-T for internal pre-submission quality control, using only the frozen reviewer snapshot for its substantive assessment.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A hash-verified artifact that independently regenerates every central number and interval from per-item records, with a complete evidence-ID crosswalk.
An executable, construct-valid definition of the commit score and its token-to-item aggregation, together with exact Brier/NLL formulas and trace-level unit tests.
A frozen, auditable filler protocol demonstrating the exact +37-token manipulation, correct pairing, fixed NFE, model/tokenizer revisions, and absence of unintended arm differences.
A common-sample, prespecified comparison between the natural and intervention contrasts with a coherent joint estimand and uncertainty analysis.
Repeated paired decodes or deterministic replay evidence separating finite-record results from decoder-run variation.
A completed primary-source positioning audit showing a meaningful gap relative to prompt-length, filler, and masked-diffusion uncertainty work.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Recovered item-level data fail to reproduce the reported means, decompositions, brackets, or pairing.
The score extraction uses outcome-irrelevant or arm-dependent aggregation, lies outside the domain assumed by NLL, or changes with answer length in a way that explains the reported contrasts.
The filler changes semantic content, formatting, answer cues, truncation, or token position beyond the declared length manipulation, or is not exactly +37 tokens under the used tokenizer.
The 400-item pool was selected after observing outcomes, contains duplicates or mismatched pairs, or materially overlaps the natural sample in an undisclosed way.
Repeated paired decodes show that the reported single realization is unstable or atypical relative to decoder-run variation.
Closer primary literature already evaluates essentially the same intervention and estimand, eliminating the claimed operation-specific distinctness.
review_limitations: The empirical records A32-E1--A32-E4, manuscript source, analysis code, and external literature were unavailable by review design, so empirical and citation claims beyond the included locks are classified as cannot_verify rather than false.
The PDF was inspected in full through text/layout extraction, metadata, font, page-count, and embedded-image checks; rasterized visual inspection was not performed.
